_why: NIGHT65 builder R (card Research/2026-10-23-wave65/cards/a2.md): a2 rebuilt from scratch as THE RANGE: the KESTREL's charged pierce. Round 2 (gg-proxy r1 BLOCKING, GG 2026-10-13 'you're encouraged to just start shooting immediately and I don't want that gameplay'): THE MARK is on THE PRESS's 2.2 m top (a double jump up), and THE RACK's three stand-ins stand on THE BREECH (2.5 m) on one line from it: spread from the door, one line only from the press's top. Wave 1's four husks hold THE BREECH beside the rack and come down THE FEED RAMP; wave 2 steps out from behind THE CARTRIDGE STACK on the west. Every piece has a job and a why.

row.name: 1.2 KESTREL
row.verb36: fire (tap), charge (hold: pierces): charge on the entry run, from THE MARK THE RACK on THE BREECH is one line (one pierce breaks its 8 s hold); then THE FEED RAMP's file of husks down the same line; THE PRESS and its pad the high line after (NIGHT65 R, THE RANGE; NIGHT66 R round 1)

standIns36.why: THE RACK (NIGHT66 R round 1, plan a2; round 2: two stand-ins): the first of two stand-ins on THE BREECH in a file in depth on THE RANGE LINE (from (0, -38) at about 18 deg east of north): from the entry run the two stand one behind the other, so one charged shot kills both and wave 1 comes at once; a tap never hurts them (Combat.cs:1464), so a refuser waits out their 8 s hold (teach46 standInHoldS). Round 2's three-body rack (0.85 m apart): skip v2 printed the verb-aware pilot's first charged shot hitting 2 bodies on 9 of 10 seeds and 3 on 1, so the third held wave 1 for a second charge; with two, the first charge breaks the hold
THE RACK (NIGHT66 R round 2): the second stand-in, 0.85 m deeper on THE RANGE LINE (round 1's 1.5 m spacing lined up only within about 1.3 m of the line; at 0.85 m within about 2.5 m either side)

row.lessons_why: NIGHT66 R round 2 (the lead's round-1 finding: reward the verb's first use on the entry line): the room's second lesson is every body down, THE RACK included (husksDead 8: the two stand-ins and the six husks; Lesson25 counts the room's kills from its start). A stand-in dies only to the charged shot (standIns31) or a shot from a wall ride (Combat.cs:1464), so the lesson is the charge the room teaches (teach35 l1.charge). A player who never charges gets the fight's last wave again (design.n25.lesson top-ups, at most 2 under rooms43, never a locked door) and the room clears on that kill count: refusing costs time, not a wall

frames52._why: NIGHT65 R: a157's poses for THE RANGE (feet x, y, z, yaw deg, pitch rad): entry = just inside d1, the press left with its cyan top, the breech and its rack and ramp ahead-right; mid = on THE MARK (the press's top) down the rack's line; high = on THE BREECH back over the room to the door

row.line65_why: NIGHT66 R round 1 (plan a2): THE RANGE LINE from the entry run (its first segment is the pierce's aim: from (0, 1, -38) to (1.83, 1.78, -43.71), 7.4 deg up, through the rack's three aim points), then up THE PRESS (a double jump), THE PRESS PAD's arc to THE BREECH, off its west edge to the exit; every segment kept out of the solids (tour65's round-1 WARN at the old frame 7, feet under THE FEED RAMP, is gone with the old last leg)
row.waveNodes43_why: NIGHT65 R (card a2): wave 1's four husks hold THE BREECH round THE RACK, in view from THE PRESS's east flank (opening held), and come down THE FEED RAMP (or off the breech's edges); wave 2's two step out from behind THE CARTRIDGE STACK on the west (both nodes in the stack's shadow from THE MARK's eye on the press's top, body and head, with the stack at 2.4 m)

boxes.why: THE BREECH (deck 2.5 m, NIGHT65 R): THE RACK's ledge (round 2) and wave 1's, in the north-east corner, in view from the press's flank (opening held); the husks come off it down THE FEED RAMP (or its 2.5 m edges); the high ground after (a double jump reaches it)

THE FEED STEP (deck 2.5 m, NIGHT65 R round 3): THE BREECH's south-west corner carried 1 m west and 0.5 m south, so THE FEED RAMP's top (on the rack's line) lands flat on it and the walkers step onto the breech (the validator's 'enemies reach every tier')

THE PRESS (hull 2.2 m, NIGHT65 R; round 2, gg-proxy r1: THE MARK on its top; round 3, the level-design review r2: 2 m longer to the north, so THE PRESS PAD's disc sits 2 m clear of THE MARK and a landing or a step during the 0.9 s charge never throws you off): the KESTREL's firing step, a double jump up (2.7 m reach): from its top THE RACK on THE BREECH is one line; the foothold (R5: 7.5-11 m from the door's centre, free-standing) and the gun room's landmark (its die on the south face); the cover you step behind when wave 2 comes from the west

THE CARTRIDGE STACK (hull 2.4 m, NIGHT65 R; round 2: 1.8 -> 2.4 m for the press-top eye): hides wave 2's two nodes from THE MARK on the press's top (the eye's rays to their bodies and heads meet its east face inside z -50..-48.5 under its top), so wave 2 steps out from the west side: a front shift, not a spawn behind

ramps.why: THE FEED RAMP (NIGHT65 R; round 3, the level-design review r2: 'the feed ramp's file comes down 9 m east, broadside, since the mark moved and the ramp did not'): turned onto THE RACK's own line, 2.5 m over 6.5 m from THE BREECH's south-west corner down toward THE PRESS: the walkers' climb route, and the husks' file comes down the line THE MARK's charged shot runs along (the second pierce from the same spot, after the rack)

pads.why: THE PRESS PAD (NIGHT65 R round 2, the level-design review's hand-off): on THE PRESS's north half, behind THE MARK: after the pierce from the mark, it throws you 13 m over the floor onto THE BREECH among wave 1's husks, so the line stays off the floor (press -> pad -> breech -> the feed ramp's file)
